overviewHtml:
This ungraded knowledge check assesses your understanding of enactivism and 4E cognition. You'll be asked about enaction, the three varieties of enactivism, the four E's, the parity principle, and the coupling-constitution objection.

Note: Use this to test yourself, review the feedback on any questions you miss, and retry until you feel confident before moving forward.

forms.stemHtml: What does enaction, as The Embodied Mind defines it, hold about cognition?

options.html: It is the representation of a world with pregiven features
options.text: It is the representation of a world with pregiven features
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. That's the cognitivist view the authors reject.

options.html: It is embodied action that brings forth a world
options.text: It is embodied action that brings forth a world
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Organism and world specify each other through sensorimotor activity.

options.html: It is the projection of the mind's order onto the world
options.text: It is the projection of the mind's order onto the world
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. That's the idealist position the middle way rejects.

options.html: It is the processing of signals inside the brain alone
options.text: It is the processing of signals inside the brain alone
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Enaction treats cognition as embodied action, not as brain-bound processing.

forms.stemHtml: Which variety of enactivism holds that basic cognition involves no mental content at all?

options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Autopoietic enactivism grounds cognition in self-production and sense-making.
Sorry, that's incorrect. Sensorimotor enactivism treats perceiving as mastery of sensorimotor contingencies.
Correct! Hutto and Myin argue that content arises only with language and social practices.
Sorry, that's incorrect. Extended functionalism isn't a variety of enactivism, and it doesn't deny content.

forms.stemHtml: Which of the following accurately state claims in the 4E family? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: Embodied: the body's form and capacities shape cognition
options.text: Embodied: the body's form and capacities shape cognition
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Cognition depends on more than the brain.

options.html: Embedded: cognition relies on structures in the environment
options.text: Embedded: cognition relies on structures in the environment
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Those structures remain outside the cognitive process itself.

options.html: Extended: external resources can be part of cognitive processes
options.text: Extended: external resources can be part of cognitive processes
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Clark and Chalmers extend this even to beliefs.

options.html: Embedded: external resources are always part of the mind
options.text: Embedded: external resources are always part of the mind
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The embedded claim keeps the environment outside the cognitive process.

options.html: Enactive: cognition represents a pregiven world accurately
options.text: Enactive: cognition represents a pregiven world accurately
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Enactivism rejects the idea of a pregiven world to be represented.

forms.stemHtml: What is the name of Clark and Chalmers's principle that if a part of the world functions as a process we would count as cognitive if it were done in the head, then it's part of the cognitive process? Enter two words.

options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Location alone doesn't decide what counts as cognitive.

forms.defaultFeedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The answer is "parity principle."

forms.stemHtml: What is Adams and Aizawa's main objection to the extended mind thesis?

options.html: That notebooks are too unreliable to store beliefs
options.text: That notebooks are too unreliable to store beliefs
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Their objection concerns the inference from coupling to constitution.

options.html: That the mind is identical to the body
options.text: That the mind is identical to the body
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Their objection concerns the inference from coupling to constitution.

options.html: That extension would make cognition too slow
options.text: That extension would make cognition too slow
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Their objection concerns the inference from coupling to constitution.

options.html: That causal coupling doesn't make a resource cognitive
options.text: That causal coupling doesn't make a resource cognitive
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! They call the inference from coupling to constitution a fallacy.

title: Enactivism and 4E Cognition
